content.text: The root cause is clear. Let me verify the total width of all cards to confirm.

I now have a complete picture of the bug.

**Root cause identified:** The project cards row is a `flex` container with `flex-wrap: nowrap`. The third card's title — "InfrastructureMonitoringDashboardForProductionServices" — is a single long unbroken string (no spaces/hyphens). The title element has `white-space: nowrap`, and the flex items have `min-width: auto` (the default), which prevents them from shrinking below their content's intrinsic width. Because that one card's title forces it to be ~478px wide (vs ~100-180px for the others), the total row width exceeds the viewport, pushing the last 3 cards off-screen.

ROOT_CAUSE: The project card title element has `white-space: nowrap` and the flex item has the default `min-width: auto`, so the long unbroken title string "InfrastructureMonitoringDashboardForProductionServices" (card index 2) prevents the flex item from shrinking, forcing the row of 8 `flex-wrap: nowrap` cards to overflow the viewport by ~378px.
EVIDENCE: `evaluate_javascript` showed the flex container has `flex-wrap: nowrap`, the title div has `white-space: nowrap`, and card 2's title "InfrastructureMonitoringDashboardForProductionServices" renders at 444px wide (vs ~70-143px for other titles), making that card 478px and causing the last 3 cards (indices 5-7) to extend past the 1280px viewport (rightmost card reaching x=1602).
CONFIDENCE: high
COULD_NOT_SEE: nothing
